thread:
emily-finops: Quick check  vendor sent invoice from Ireland but included VAT. Vendor claims they're VAT-registered IE9876543V. Should we pay VAT or apply reverse charge?

tarek-tax: For B2B EU cross-border services, if our Irish customer VAT ID validates and the supplier is EU-registered supplying services to a business, reverse charge applies. We need the supplier's VAT ID and a VIES validation snapshot. Also confirm the invoice shows "reverse charge" wording or we'll ask for corrected invoice.

jo-cs: Customer (EdgeGate Ltd) provided their VAT ID earlier, it's IRL1234567A. Do we have VIES proof on file?

acct-pay: I looked: we have a copy of the invoice but no VIES screenshot. Vendor-bot recorded invoice INV-2026-0789. Link: https://billing.redwood/invoices/INV-2026-0789

emily-finops: If vendor included VAT and reverse charge should apply, can we ask for a credit note? Or can we deduct VAT and pay vendor net?

tarek-tax: Standard: request credit note + new invoice referencing reverse charge. If vendor refuses, we can still process payment but need to document attempts and tax opinion. For accounting, prefer credit note.

jo-cs: Customer prefers quick payment. Can we fast-track credit note request template?

acct-pay: I'll send vendor an email template: request VIES screenshot, issue credit note referencing original invoice, include wording "Reverse charge  Article 44 VAT Directive". Ticket created: FIN-5012.

vendor-bot: Vendor replied: "We charged VAT mistakenly, will issue credit note and reissue without VAT. ETA 3 business days."

emily-finops: Perfect. Tarek, can you confirm audit notes we should attach?

tarek-tax: Attach original invoice, vendor VIES validation, email exchange, reissued invoice/credit note. Tag FIN-5012. Then close.

acct-pay: Will update ticket and follow up if no reissue in 3 days.

emily-finops: Thanks all. Closing once FIN-5012 resolved.
